newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares close higher, seen rangebound.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares close higher, seen rangebound.

text.p: Austrian shares closed Wednesday's trading session on a firm note, but failed to hold on to the day's highs after an early bull run fizzled out amid a lack of follow-up orders, traders said.

The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 4.18 points or 0.36 percent to finish the day at 1,170.95, below the day's high of 1,178.47 points. Among its constituents, eleven gainers outnumbered nine decliners, two issues closed unchanged.
Market participants said they expect the index to remain trapped in a narrow range ahead of Friday's expiry of April futures and options contracts.
"There's some strong support at 1,160 points," said one trader. "But we can't get above 1,180 points either."
Steelmaker Boehler-Uddeholm led the day's winners, rising 2.41 percent to 849 schillings. "Boehler are in demand and they'll continue to be in demand for a while," said a trader.
Engineering group VA Technologie rose 40 schillings to close at 1,740 after releasing a strong set of 1996 earnings and promising more good news for the current year.

On the negative side, chip maker AMS lost 1.19 percent to close at 999 and traders said they expected the share to slide further over the next days. "After AMS broke through key support at 1,000, some investors panicked," said one trader.
Airport operator Flughafen Wien was up 9.5 schilllings at 518.50 ahead of the release of 1996 earnings data due on Thursday.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, ATX contracts for April delivery fell 2.1 points to 1,169.2 on volume of 2,892 contracts. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
